countersignature_20260913.reason: Source (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:72-87, SM15) states four clauses about chi_{ijk}(P) = sgn det(mu_j - mu_i, mu_k - mu_i) (def:chirotope, lines 63-70) for a labelled tuple P and all i,j,k in Z/n, with no genericity or nonzero-edge hypothesis. The Lean definitions denote the printed objects exactly: SM.det u v = u.1*v.2 - u.2*v.1 (Polygon.lean:16) is det(u,v) = u_1v_2 - u_2v_1 (source line 5); SM.bracket u v = u.2*v.1 - u.1*v.2 (Polygon.lean:17) is the main text's [u,v] = u_2v_1 - u_1v_2 (source line 14, lemma (ii)); SM.edge P i = P(i+1) - P i (Polygon.lean:49) is l_i; SM.chi (Chirotope.lean:10-11) is sgn det(mu_j - mu_i, mu_k - mu_i) with Mathlib's SignType.sign, which is exactly sgn: R -> {-1,0,1} (sign_apply); SM.turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1) (Chirotope.lean:13-14) is tau_i; SM.leftTurns counts turn P i = 1, matching l(P). SM.chi_basic (Chirotope.lean:121-134) takes an arbitrary P : LabelledTuple n = ZMod n -> R x R and asserts: (i) sign change under all three transpositions (lines 122-124), invariance under a cyclic permutation (line 125; the other cyclic rotation follows by applying it twice), and vanishing for all three coincidence patterns (lines 126-128); (ii) chi P i j k = sign (bracket (P j - P i) (P j - P k)) (line 129), the printed formula with the same argument order; (iii) chi P i (i+1) k = sign (det (edge P i) (P k - P i)) (line 130), the printed formula, plus the naming convention via strictlyLeft/strictlyRight (lines 131-132, defs at 24-28: positive/negative det(l_i, x - mu_i)), which is exactly 'sign +1 = strictly left, -1 = strictly right'; (iv) turn P i = sign (det (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i)) (line 133) and turn P i = 1 iff 0 < det(l_{i-1}, l_i) (line 134), the printed identity and the left-turn naming. Same domain (labelled tuples, cyclic indices), same universal quantifiers, same conclusions, no inserted hypotheses, nothing vacuous. SM15 rewording: only clause (iii)'s naming sentence changed, now conditioned on l_i != 0 (CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md section 1: wording only, formula unchanged). The accepted Lean statement matches the SM15 text: the formula clause is stated verbatim, and the strictlyLeft/strictlyRight predicates are total but agree with the source's convention wherever the source makes it (l_i != 0); for a zero edge both predicates are false and chi = 0, so the iff clauses hold trivially and assert nothing beyond the source on that degenerate locus. No restatement is needed for SM15. After forming this judgement I read work/reviews/lem-chi-basic.json; it reaches the same conclusion and its recorded file hashes match the files I read.
